content: Esomeprazole sodium is prescribed to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), a condition where stomach acid flows backward into the esophagus, causing heartburn and potential damage to the esophageal lining. It is used to alleviate GERD symptoms, promote healing of the esophagus, and prevent further esophageal damage. Additionally, esomeprazole is used to reduce the risk of developing stomach or intestinal ulcers in individuals taking nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). It is also combined with other medications to treat and prevent the recurrence of stomach ulcers caused by Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection. Furthermore, esomeprazole is used to manage conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and works by decreasing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Esomeprazole is available as a delayed-release capsule, which releases the medication in the intestine to prevent breakdown by stomach acids. It can be taken orally or mixed with water for administration through a feeding tube. It is also available as granules that can be mixed with water for oral consumption or feeding tube use. Typically, esomeprazole is taken once daily, at least one hour before a meal. For certain conditions involving excessive stomach acid production, it may be taken twice daily. It is important to take esomeprazole at the same time(s) each day and follow the prescription label instructions carefully. Do not take more or less of the medication or use it for a longer duration than prescribed. Swallow the capsules whole without splitting, chewing, or crushing them. If swallowing the capsule is difficult, you can mix the contents with one tablespoon of cool, soft applesauce and consume the mixture immediately without chewing the pellets. Do not save the mixture for later use. To prepare the granules, place one tablespoon (15 mL) of water in a cup, empty the granules into the water, stir, and let the mixture thicken for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir again and drink the mixture within 30 minutes. If any residue remains, add more water, stir, and drink immediately. Both the granules and capsule contents can be administered through a feeding tube. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for specific instructions if you have a feeding tube. It may take several weeks or longer to experience the full benefits of esomeprazole. Contact your doctor if your symptoms worsen or do not improve during this time. Continue taking esomeprazole even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Before taking esomeprazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to esomeprazole, other PPIs (e.g., omeprazole, lansoprazole), or any ingredients in the medication. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, as certain drugs may interact with esomeprazole. Notify your doctor if you have a history of low magnesium levels or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Older adults, particularly those over 50, may have an increased risk of severe diarrhea caused by bacteria or fractures of the wrist, hip, or spine when taking PPIs. Discuss these risks with your doctor. You may take antacids with esomeprazole if needed, but consult your doctor for recommendations on which antacid to use and how to take it. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you can continue your normal diet while taking esomeprazole. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Esomeprazole may cause side effects. Common side effects include headache, nausea, gas, constipation, and dry mouth. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects requiring immediate medical attention include blistering or peeling skin, hives, rash, itching, difficulty breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face or extremities, hoarseness, irregular or rapid heartbeat, excessive tiredness, dizziness, muscle spasms, uncontrollable shaking, seizures, severe diarrhea with watery stools, stomach pain, or fever. Long-term or high-dose use of PPIs may increase the risk of fractures. Discuss this risk with your doctor. Report any unusual problems while taking esomeprazole to your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store esomeprazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual collapses or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include confusion, drowsiness, blurred vision, rapid heartbeat, nausea, sweating, flushing, headache, and dry mouth. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory while taking esomeprazole. Do not share your medication with others. Maintain a written list of all medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, and bring it to all medical appointments or hospital visits. This information is also essential in emergencies.
